title: Can AI speed up operational due diligence on fund managers?
description: How a family office can use AI to line up fund managers' questionnaire answers and flag gaps, while people make every approve or veto call.
verdict: Operational due diligence (ODD) tests whether a fund manager's business is trustworthy, and 30% of investors lack a dedicated team.[^15][^1]
AI earns its keep lining up each manager's answers and flagging gaps, since every manager answers differently.[^19][^6]
By our count, only about 40% of the Institutional Limited Partners Association (ILPA) questionnaire lines up without judgment.[^6][^7]
A questionnaire is the manager's own account, so people still confirm facts and make the veto call.[^14][^7]
Build a light grid for a few managers a year, and buy a platform when reviews pile up.[^1][^18]

summary: Operational due diligence (ODD) checks whether a fund manager's business, not its strategy, can be trusted.[^15][^6] AI pulls each manager's due diligence questionnaire (DDQ) answers into one grid and flags what is missing.[^18][^19] Judgment still decides, because a DDQ is the manager's own account.[^7][^14]

answers.human-role: People keep every call on the manager: the committee votes, and the chief operating officer (COO) or chief investment officer (CIO) owns the ODD view.[^1][^16] Counsel signs off the legal terms.[^16]
answers.team-after: Your team moves from copying answers into spreadsheets to chasing gaps, confirming facts with outside parties and writing the judgment.[^19][^14]
answers.example: An illustrative office comparing three private credit managers gets one grid of lined-up answers, a gap list and a list of claims to confirm.[^6][^20]
answers.table-1: DiligenceVault, CENTRL, Ping and Penguin Capital read DDQs or fund documents, and every speed figure below is the vendor's own claim.[^18][^19]
answers.table-2: Ask private equity managers for the ILPA DDQ 2.0 and hedge fund managers for the Alternative Investment Management Association (AIMA) questionnaire, plus ILPA's reporting and performance templates.[^6][^8]
answers.recipes: Offices that vet a handful of managers a year should build a grid on the ILPA template, and busier offices should buy a diligence platform.[^6][^1]
answers.own-data: About 40% of the ILPA questionnaire's numbered questions take answers a machine can line up without judgment, by our count of 175 of 436.[^6][^7]
answers.rules: No rule tells a single family office how to vet managers, and the rule that would have forced standard quarterly fund statements was vacated in 2024.[^25][^11]
answers.benchmark: Rerun one finished manager review with AI, then count the answers it lined up right, the gaps it caught and the gaps it missed.[^19][^24]
answers.what-goes-wrong: AI-assisted diligence goes wrong when a tidy grid is taken as proof, because the grid only repeats what the manager wrote.[^7][^13]
answers.buy-or-build: Buy a platform when reviews pile up past what one person can read, and build a light grid when you vet only a few managers a year.[^1][^18]
answers.something-else: Pick something else when you are buying a company rather than a fund stake, or when an outside adviser already runs manager diligence for you.[^29][^2]

humanRole: Investment committee: votes on the commitment and its size. In the Standards Board for Alternative Investments (SBAI) survey, the committee is the main reader of ODD findings.[^1]
COO or CIO: owns the ODD view where there is no dedicated team. In SBAI's survey, 54% of such investors put ODD under the CIO and 23% under the COO.[^1]

Operations lead: calls the administrator and auditor directly instead of trusting the questionnaire.[^14][^15] In Deutsche Bank's survey, 92% of investors named the administrator the most important provider to contact.[^14]
Outside counsel: reviews the limited partnership agreement (LPA) and side letters, and signs off the legal terms.[^16][^23]
teamAfter: Analysts stop retyping answers and start chasing the gaps the grid shows.[^19][^18]
The operations lead spends the saved time on confirmations, visits and background checks.[^14][^15]
The memo writer keeps the judgment: CENTRL's case study says the client kept analyst time for judgment-heavy work.[^19]
Where AI changed tasks, 66% of US firms use it only to help staff, and AI-related job losses hit only 2% of AI-using firms.[^26]

example.input: Illustrative: a 12-person single family office is weighing three private credit managers for one commitment. Each sends the ILPA DDQ, audited financials, a draft LPA and side letters, about 300 pages apiece. Each answers in its own format.
example.output: One grid: a row per ILPA question, a column per manager, each cell linked to its page. A gap list: Manager B left the key-person questions blank, and Manager C's administrator is an affiliate. A confirm list for the COO: the administrator, the auditor and the fee terms in each side letter.

recipes.name: 1. A few managers a year: a grid on the ILPA template
recipes.when: Offices with no dedicated ODD team, like many smaller investors in SBAI's survey.[^1] Interest runs ahead of use: 35% of North American offices want AI help choosing managers, and around a quarter use it.[^5]
flow: COO: send every manager the ILPA DDQ 2.0 and its document list
AI: pull each manager's answers into one grid, each cell linked to its page
Analyst: check every blank and every 'not found' by hand
Operations lead: confirm the administrator, auditor and cash controls directly
COO: write the approve, condition or veto view for the investment committee
recipes.cost: The ILPA DDQ 2.0 is free, so the main cost is staff time on gaps and confirmations.[^6][^14]

recipes.name: 2. Many managers a year: a diligence platform
recipes.when: Offices with a steady flow of private equity, credit and hedge fund reviews, where reading long document packs is the bottleneck.[^19][^3]
flow: COO: load the office's questionnaire and red-flag rules into the platform
Platform AI: fill answers from each manager's existing DDQ and send back only the gaps
Analyst: approve each extracted answer against its source page
AI: check DDQ claims against the data room and filings, and list mismatches
Operations lead: confirm with the administrator and auditor, and run background checks
Investment committee: decide, with the ODD view in the memo
recipes.cost: DiligenceVault, CENTRL and Ping publish no price on the pages we read.[^18][^19][^20]

ownData.title: How much of the ILPA questionnaire lines up across managers?
ownData.intro: We read ILPA's free DDQ 2.0 on 28 Nov 2026 and sorted every numbered question by the answer it asks for.[^6] A yes/no box, a table or a single fact can be lined up by a machine. A written answer needs a person to weigh it.[^7]
headers: Lines up without judgment, our count
ownData.note: Method: we parsed the text and counted 436 numbered questions, with 158 yes/no boxes, 5 tables and 12 hand-picked single facts. Limits: four question numbers were lost in our text copy, and a manager can add prose to any yes/no box. The data templates in Appendices B to H also line up, but we did not count them.

rules.name: SEC Private Fund Advisers rules (vacated)
rules.what: The Fifth Circuit struck down the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) rules that would have forced quarterly statements on fees and performance.[^11][^12] Standard fund reporting now rests on ILPA's voluntary templates, so ask for them in the side letter.[^10]

rules.name: Form ADV, 17 CFR 275.204-1
rules.what: A registered manager files Form ADV, the adviser registration form, and Part 2A Item 9 carries its disciplinary history.[^15] Check that Form ADV, the offering memo and the DDQ answers agree, since a mismatch is a red flag.[^15]

rules.name: Family office rule, 17 CFR 275.202(a)(11)(G)-1
rules.what: A single family office that serves only family is not an investment adviser under the rule.[^25] No regulator sets its diligence standard, so the office's written policy is the standard.

howToTest: Pick one manager review you finished last year, with the DDQ, the documents and your final memo.

Record today's numbers: days from DDQ received to decision, and hours spent building the comparison. In SBAI's survey of 44 institutional investors, 41% don't always have enough time for a review.[^1]
Have AI build the grid from the raw DDQ and documents, without your memo.
Score every cell against your own grid: right, wrong or missed.
Check every 'not found' by hand. In the Contract Understanding Atticus Dataset (CUAD) benchmark, 70 to 80% of clause checks have no matching clause, so absence is the usual answer.[^24]
Test questions that span documents on their own: in the Vals legal test, tools struggled most when answers sat across several documents.[^22]
Price the lift: hours saved times loaded cost, plus weeks cut from the cycle. CENTRL's client reports DDQ cycles cut from 10 weeks to 6, by the vendor's account.[^19]
watchOuts: Taking the grid as proof: ILPA says yes/no answers give only a top-level view, not a basis for investing.[^7] Confirm key facts with the administrator and auditor directly.[^14]
Missed clauses: in contract benchmarks most clause checks find no clause, so a 'not found' may really sit in an appendix or side letter.[^24] Have a person check every gap.[^22]
Mixed bases: returns with and without subscription lines, or gross and net, lined up in one column.[^9] Label the basis in every cell, as ILPA's Performance Template does.[^10]
Missing the costly risk: Capco put half of over 100 hedge fund failures down to operational risk.[^13] Castle Hall counted $80 billion of investor losses across 327 operational failures.[^13]
Pressure to approve: just under a quarter of SBAI respondents have felt pressed to approve despite known risks.[^1] Write the veto rule down before the review starts.[^15]

faq.q: What is operational due diligence in private equity?
faq.a: Operational due diligence checks a private equity manager's business: its controls, administrator, valuation, compliance and people.[^15][^6] Investment diligence, which judges the strategy and track record, runs beside it.[^15][^16]

faq.q: Is fund operational due diligence the same as M&A due diligence?
faq.a: No, because fund ODD vets a manager you hand money to, while mergers and acquisitions (M&A) diligence vets a company you buy.[^15] For acquisitions, read our AI due diligence guide.[^29]

faq.q: What goes on an operational due diligence checklist?
faq.a: An ODD checklist covers ownership, people, compliance, valuation, cash controls, service providers and legal terms.[^15] ILPA's DDQ 2.0 spreads these over 20 sections and lists 89 documents to request.[^6]

faq.q: How long does operational due diligence take?
faq.a: Most initial ODD reviews take two to eight weeks, says a Deutsche Bank survey of investors.[^14] Family offices take two weeks to twelve months for the whole manager decision.[^16][^17]

faq.q: Can AI fill in or compare a DDQ for us?
faq.a: Yes, AI can pull each manager's answers into one grid and flag blanks, but a person must check every gap.[^19][^7] Vendor tools cite the source page for each answer, so a person can check it against the page.[^18][^20]

faq.q: Should we use the ILPA DDQ or our own questionnaire?
faq.a: Start from the ILPA DDQ so answers line up across managers, then add your own follow-up questions.[^6][^7] In SBAI's survey, 59% of investors use their own questionnaire and 14% use industry templates.[^1]

buyVsBuild.buy: Buy a diligence platform when reviews pile up: SBAI found investors under $5bn use no third-party tools, while larger ones sometimes do.[^1] Vendors such as DiligenceVault claim review time falls by over 70 percent.[^18] Across US enterprise AI decision-makers, 76% of AI use cases are now bought rather than built.[^27]
buyVsBuild.build: Build a light grid when you vet a handful of managers a year.[^6] The ILPA DDQ is free, and about 40% of it lines up without judgment, by our count.[^6] For organizations MIT NANDA studied, partnered builds reached deployment about 67% of the time, against about 33% for internal ones.[^28]

pickElse: Buying a company, not a fund stake: that is M&A diligence, covered in our AI due diligence guide.[^29]

An adviser already runs manager selection: 41% of offices using outside investment advisers rely on them for due diligence and manager access.[^2] J.P. Morgan finds 80% of offices outsource part of the portfolio, including manager selection.[^4]
Your pain starts after you commit: fund statements and quarterly reports belong in our family office reporting guide.[^30]
You vet only one or two managers a year: a shared spreadsheet on the ILPA template, filled by hand, may be enough.[^6]

sources.name: Standards Board for Alternative Investments (SBAI), Operational Due Diligence Practices Survey (Apr 2024)
sources.what: Survey of 44 institutional investors with over $2tn under management, family offices among SBAI's investor members. 70% have dedicated ODD teams and the remaining 30% do not; teams of 1 to 4 people are most common. Where there is no dedicated team, 54% put ODD under the CIO or investment function, 23% under the COO or operations and 7% under the CRO. External consultants are used by 59%, and by 77% of those without a dedicated team. The Investment Committee is the primary recipient of review findings. 32% of dedicated teams have formal veto rights, and 73% of those with a veto use it rarely, once a year or less. 59% use their own bespoke DDQ; 14% use common industry templates; 18% rely on manager materials. Respondents with less than $5bn under management ($0bn-$5bn) do not use third-party data gathering tools. 41% do not always have enough time to perform an ODD review. Just under a quarter have felt pressured to approve allocations despite the risks identified. Read 28 Nov 2026.

sources.name: Citi Private Bank, 2025 Global Family Office Report
sources.what: Survey of 346 family office participants. 60% work with external investment advisors; services they rely on those advisors for include due diligence & access to managers (41%). 54% have adopted due diligence of investments as a core practice, 69% of larger offices vs 40% of those under $500 million. Read 28 Nov 2026.

sources.name: Citi Private Bank, 2026 Global Family Office Report
sources.what: Survey of 351 family offices. Benefits from AI include reducing manual work (35%), accelerating due diligence (35%) and improving decision-support quality (33%); 43% in North America report faster due diligence; 24% report no measurable impact yet. Read 28 Nov 2026.

sources.name: J.P. Morgan Private Bank, 2026 Global Family Office Report
sources.what: Survey of 333 single family offices in 30 countries. 80% of global family offices report some degree of portfolio outsourcing, such as outsourced CIOs, due diligence and manager selection. Read 28 Nov 2026.

sources.what: Survey of 155 single and private multi-family offices across the Americas (123 US). 35% would like to use AI in investment manager selection, "but only around a quarter are there". Read 28 Nov 2026.

sources.name: ILPA, Due Diligence Questionnaire 2.0 (updated Nov 2021)
sources.what: Free questionnaire from the Institutional Limited Partners Association. Its overview says rising diligence detail led to a proliferation of lengthy, customized due diligence questionnaires. 20 sections, from Firm: General Information to Diversity, Equity and Inclusion, in short form Yes/No and long form questions. Appendix A lists 89 requested documents; Appendices B to H are data templates for team members, references, third parties and technology tools, fund, portfolio investments, GP-led secondaries and credit facilities, to be sent in spreadsheet format. Zavient counted its numbered questions: 436 read, 158 yes/no boxes, 5 tables and 12 single facts, so 175 (40%) line up without judgment and 261 need a written answer, by our count. Read 28 Nov 2026.

sources.name: ILPA, DDQ 2.0 User Guide (9 Nov 2021)
sources.what: The Yes/No questions "are intended to provide LPs with a top-level view" and a framework to flag issues; LPs should review the expanded answers and their own follow-up questions before making any investment decision. Emerging managers may not have full answers on predecessor funds. Read 28 Nov 2026.

sources.name: Deutsche Bank Global Prime Finance, 2014 Operational Due Diligence Survey
sources.what: Survey of over 70 hedge fund investor entities managing over $2.72 trillion; family offices sit in the high net worth group. Emerging managers received an ODD veto in 9% of reviews and established managers in 6%. The DDQ often serves as an introduction; investors then use on-site visits and calls. Read 28 Nov 2026.

sources.name: One Constellation, Operational Due Diligence (ODD) for Fund Investors: A Guide (vendor, Nov 2026)
sources.what: ODD asks whether the business around a strategy can be trusted, separate from investment due diligence. Red flags: a single person who can release payments, a related-party administrator or valuation agent, late audits, and Form ADV, offering memo and DDQ answers that do not agree. Form ADV Part 2A Item 9 carries disciplinary information. Read 28 Nov 2026.

sources.name: MIT NANDA, The GenAI Divide: State of AI in Business 2025 (Jul 2025)
sources.what: MIT no longer hosts the report (its link now opens the NANDA project page, checked 26 Nov 2026); copy hosted by MLQ.ai. Sample: 52 organizations interviewed, survey of 153 leaders, and 300+ public AI initiatives reviewed. $30-40 billion of enterprise GenAI investment; 95% of organizations are getting zero return; just 5% of integrated AI pilots extract millions in value. Task-specific tools: 60% of organizations evaluated them, 20% piloted, 5% reached production. Over 80% of organizations explored or piloted ChatGPT or Copilot, and nearly 40% report deployment. External partnerships with customized tools reached deployment about 67% of the time vs about 33% for internal builds: 2x as likely, twice the success rate. Only 40% of companies purchased an official LLM subscription; workers at over 90% of companies surveyed use personal AI tools for work. For mission-critical work, 90% of users prefer humans. Enterprises, defined as firms with over $100 million in annual revenue, lead in pilot count but report the lowest pilot-to-scale conversion. Read 26 Nov 2026.

offer.heading: Comparing fund managers this quarter? Get a free diagnostic
offer.body: Bring one manager's DDQ and the memo you wrote on it. In 30 minutes you leave with the first step, a before-and-after measure and the questions a grid can't answer. You get it in writing, with no sales pitch.

reviews.notes: Lead problem is clear: every manager answers differently and someone must line the answers up. The human-role answer read as a comma splice; joined it with 'and'. Cut 'so the check is quick' from the DDQ FAQ, which no source backs; it now says a person checks each answer against its page.

Test plan runs on one finished review with the office's own memo as the answer key. The 'not found' step and the multi-document step match where tools fail. Recipe flows name a role on every step. No change.

Bottom line answers the title in five short bullets, and the first bullet now says 'can be trusted' instead of the vaguer 'is safe'. The last pick-else line about enterprise AI buying read off-topic; replaced it with the one-or-two-managers case and moved the Menlo figure into the buy answer.

Read as head of investment operations. The own-data table says which sections line up and which need a person, and the note is honest about four lost question numbers and the uncounted data templates. Confirm list in the example (administrator, auditor, side-letter fees) matches the job. No change.

Answers whether AI can speed manager vetting and what stays with people. The fund-versus-M&A line is plain in the title, the summary and the FAQ. Offer is concrete; no Zavient price, by decision. No change.
